children: Bitcoin gave up part of its rebound after reclaiming $60,000, slipping back below $59,000. The token had rebounded after falling into the $55,000 range during this week's sharp selloff, but failed to hold its gains as outflows from U.S. spot exchange-traded funds and concerns about further monetary tightening persisted.
Bitcoin was trading at about $58,900 in Binance's BTC/USDT spot market on Nov. 22. After recovering from its low and briefly retaking $60,000, it turned lower again and lost the $59,000 level.

Money continued to leave spot ETFs. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs posted combined net outflows of $1.1287 billion over the three days from Nov. 17 to Nov. 19, according to Farside Investors. On Nov. 19 alone, $582.3 million left the funds, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for $541.1 million of that total.

Preliminary data for Nov. 20 showed net outflows of $124.5 million, although some products had yet to be fully tallied. Based on the figures released so far, total net outflows for the week of Nov. 16 through Nov. 20 came to about $1.2453 billion. The funds posted modest net inflows at the start of the week before logging four straight days of outflows.

The macro backdrop is also weighing on sentiment. Rising U.S. Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and the possibility of additional tightening by the Federal Reserve, combined with a selloff in technology stocks, have weakened appetite for risk assets. Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, told Decrypt that higher Treasury yields, dollar strength and expectations for further Fed tightening were pressuring demand for risk assets.

Selling by investors looking to reduce holdings into the rebound is another variable. Tim Sun, senior researcher at Huobi Research, said investors could shift from buying the dip to selling into strength if the macro outlook does not improve. That, he added, could create additional selling pressure during subsequent rebounds.

The U.S. personal consumption expenditures price index for October is due on Nov. 25. The inflation gauge is closely watched by the Fed, and markets will use the release to assess the inflation trend and the likelihood of further rate increases.

title: Bitcoin Rebound Loses Steam After Selloff, With Price Back Below $59,000
